observations: The training loop uses floor division for batch count and warns that remainder data will be dropped.
Each batch runs rollouts, then the experience updater, then optional evaluation.
Retaining the tail is a declared repository adaptation, not exact upstream behavior.

batch32_keep_tail.policy_freeze: One batch across all four replicas; no within-batch memory update.
batch32_keep_tail.roster_rule: Exactly one pass over all pinned construction identities; keep the 17 and 24 input tails. No outcome-based selection.
batch32_keep_tail.checkpoint_semantics: M1 denotes after R01C (20 batch opportunities); M2 denotes after A (54 cumulative batch opportunities).
batch32_keep_tail.evaluation: Fold B1080 full roster for each frozen arm, never a 32-input effectiveness claim.

limits: No randomized execution order or concrete batch rosters have been registered.
Existing held full-cohort actor cells cannot execute a minibatch schedule unchanged.
Memory construction must accumulate every prior batch while later actor cohorts remain disjoint from earlier experience sources.
All eligible group operations remain in their batch; no top-k filtering to pass context fit.
Batch count is an upper bound on update contacts, not proof that every batch yields usable feedback or accepted memory.
Official scoring runs once per complete actor manifest; a minibatch manifest defines its full training population and is not an arbitrary shard of an evaluation manifest.
The 32-input choice is a prospective adaptation, not an upstream default or empirical optimum.
Real service capacity, memory-content limits and registered contact budgets remain required.
